e9fccc2b4a.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in āśrēṣā karkaṭaḥ, center-to-center separation 0°30′34.74″.
e9fccc2b4a.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°30′34.74″, 0°30′27.42″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at āśrēṣā-3 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°44′25.13″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -2.04, elongation 1°45′15.46″ W). śukraḥ at āśrēṣā-3 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 1°13′50.39″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 1°14′58.57″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
e9fccc2b4a.s:
ಭಾವಾಭಾವಾಯ ಲೋಕಾನಾಂ ಕಲ್ಪನೇಯಂ ಪ್ರದರ್ಶಿತಾ।  
ಸ್ವಮಾರ್ಗಗಾಃ ಪ್ರಯಾನ್ತ್ಯೇತೇ ದೂರಮನ್ಯೋನ್ಯಮಾಶ್ರಿತಾಃ॥  
--ಸೂರ್ಯಸಿದ್ಧಾನ್ತೇ  
  
ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಂ ಗ್ರಹಭಿನ್ನಭಂ ತ್ಯಜ ಶುಭೇ ಯೌದ್ಧಂ ತಥೋತ್ಪಾತಭಮ್।  
--ಮುಹೂರ್ತಚಿನ್ತಾಮಣೌ (ನಾರದಸಂಹಿತಾನುಸಾರೇಣ)

ea122ef076.d: The three days around the Ashtaka Shraaddha of  mārgaśīrṣa, pauṣa and māgha month are anadhyayana days, where one is not supposed to learn the Vedas.
ea122ef076.s:
ಮಾರ್ಗಶೀರ್ಷೇ ತಥಾ ಪೌಷೇ ಮಾಘಮಾಸೇ ತಥೈವ ಚ॥೭೬॥  
ತಿಸ್ರೋಽಷ್ಟಕಾಃ ಸಮಾಖ್ಯಾತಾಃ ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇಷು ಸೂರಿಭಿಃ।  
---ಶ್ರೀಕೂರ್ಮಪುರಾಣೇ ಷಟ್‌ಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಮುಪರಿವಿಭಾಗೇ ಚತುರ್ದಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯೇ

ea19476994.d: Observed on the first Friday following the transit of Sun into tulārāśī. Three Vratas are very special for Subrahmanya---this one, the regular kr̥ttikā vratam, and skandaṣaṣṭhivratam.
ea19476994.s:
ಅನ್ಯದ್ವ್ರತಂ ಪ್ರವಕ್ಷ್ಯಾಮಿ ಸುಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣ್ಯಸ್ಯ ವೈ ದ್ವಿಜಾಃ।  
ತುಲಾರಾಶಿಂ ಗತೇ ಸೂರ್ಯ ಪೂರ್ವಸ್ಮಿನ್ ಭೃಗುವಾಸರೇ॥೧॥  
ಸಮುತ್ಥಾಯ ಶುಚಿರ್ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಪ್ರಾತರೇವ ಷಡಾನನಮ್।  
ಧ್ಯಾತ್ವಾ ಹೃದಬ್ಜನಿಲಯೇ ನಿತ್ಯಕರ್ಮ ಸಮಾಪ್ಯ ಚ॥೨॥  
ವ್ರತಂ ಚರೇದ್ವಿಧಾನೇನ ಸರ್ವಪಾಪಹರಂ ಪರಮ್।  
ಕೃತ್ತಿಕಾವ್ರತಮನ್ಯಚ್ಚ ಸ್ಕನ್ದಷಷ್ಠಿವ್ರತಂ ಪರಮ್॥೩॥  
ವ್ರತಾನಿ ತ್ರೀಣಿ ಯೇ ಮರ್ತ್ಯಾಶ್ಚರನ್ತ್ಯಾಗಮಮಾರ್ಗತಃ।  
ತೇ ಭುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ವಿಪುಲಾನ್ ಭೋಗಾನನ್ತೇ ಮೋಕ್ಷಂ ಗುಹಾಜ್ಞಯಾ॥೪॥  
ಬ್ರಹ್ಮವಿಷ್ಣ್ವಾದಯೋ ದೇವಾಶ್ಚರಿತ್ವೈತಾನಿ ಭೂಸುರಾಃ।  
ಜಘ್ನುರ್ದೈತ್ಯಾನ್ಮಹಾಘೋರಾನ್ರಣಮಧ್ಯಗತಾನ್ ಪುರಾ॥೫॥  
ಕರ್ತೃತ್ವಂ ಚ ದಿಶಾಂ ಪ್ರಾಪುರ್ದಿಕ್ಪಾಲಾಃ ಪುನರಪ್ಯುತ।  
ಮುಚುಕುನ್ದೋ ಮಹೀಪಾಲಃ ಶತ್ರೂಞ್ಜಿತ್ವಾ ರಣೇ ಪುರಾ॥೬॥  
ಗಾಣಾಧಿಪತ್ಯಂ ಸಮ್ಪ್ರಾಪ ಚರಿತ್ವೈತಾನಿ ಭೂಸುರಾಃ।  
ನಾರದಪ್ರಮುಖಾಃ ಪೂರ್ವೇ ತಾಪಸಾನಾಮಧೀಶ್ವರಾಃ॥೭॥  
ನಿತ್ಯತ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಾಪುರತುಲಂ ಪುನರಾವೃತ್ತಿದುರ್ಲಭಮ್।  
ಪುತ್ರಾನಾಯುಃ ಪುರಾ ಕೇಚಿದಪುತ್ರಾ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣೋತ್ತಮಾಃ॥೮॥  
ಐಶ್ವರ್ಯಂ ಜ್ಞಾನಯೋಗಾಂಶ್ಚ ಮೋಕ್ಷಂ ಚಾಪುಃ ಪುರಾ ಪರೇ।  
ತ್ರಿಷ್ವೇತೇಷು ವ್ರತಂ ಚೈಕಂ ಯಶ್ಚರೇದ್ಗುಹಸಮ್ಮತಮ್॥೯॥  
ಸ ಲಬ್ಧ್ವಾ ವಾಞ್ಛಿತಂ ಸರ್ವಂ ಶಿವಲೋಕಮನುತ್ತಮಮ್।  
ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ಮೋಕ್ಷಂ ವ್ರಜತ್ಯನ್ತೇ ಗುಹಸ್ಯೈವ ಪ್ರಸಾದತಃ॥೧೦॥  
ತ್ರೀಣಿ ವ್ರತಾನಿ ಯೋ ಮರ್ತ್ಯಶ್ಚರತಿ ಸ್ಕನ್ದಸಮ್ಮತಮ್।  
ಮಾಹಾತ್ಮ್ಯಂ ತಸ್ಯ ಕೋ ವೇತ್ತಿ ಗುಹತುಲ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಭೂಸುರಾಃ॥೧೧॥  
ಯ ಇಮಂ ಪಠತೇಽಧ್ಯಾಯಂ ಯಃ ಶೃಣೋತಿ ಗುಹಪ್ರಿಯಮ್।  
ಸ ಭುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ವಿಪುಲಾನ್ ಭೋಗಾನ್ ಮೋಕ್ಷಂ ಯಾತಿ ಮಹೀಸುರಾಃ॥   
ಶ್ರೀ ಸ್ಕಾನ್ದೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಶಙ್ಕರಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಂ ಶಿವರಹಸ್ಯಖಣ್ಡೇ ಉಪದೇಶಕಾಣ್ಡೇ ಸಪ್ತತ್ರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯೇ

ea3004339c.b: Observed on Śukla-Prathamā tithi of Āṣāḍhaḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
ea3004339c.d: Āṣāḍha-māsaḥ begins today --- In the Mahābhārata, it is said that one who observes a disciplined ekabhakta (one meal a day) fast throughout the month of Āṣāḍha, without lethargy (atandritaḥ), will be blessed with abundant grain, wealth, and many children. In the Vāmana Purāṇa, it is said that, to please Vāmana in the month of Āṣāḍha, one should offer — with devotion — a pair of sandals, an umbrella, salt, and āmalaka fruits.
ea3004339c.s:
ಆಷಾಢಕೃತ್ಯಂ ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇ---  
ಆಷಾಢಮೇಕಭಕ್ತೇನ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ತ್ವಾ ಮಾಸಮತನ್ದ್ರಿತಃ।  
ಬಹುಧಾನ್ಯೋ ಬಹುಧನೋ ಬಹುಪುತ್ರಶ್ಚ ಜಾಯತೇ॥  
ವಾಮನಪುರಾಣೇ---  
ಉಪಾನದ್ಯುಗಲಂ ಛತ್ರಂ ಲವಣಾಮಲಕಾನಿ ಚ।  
ಆಷಾಢೇ ವಾಮನಪ್ರೀತ್ಯೈ ದಾತವ್ಯಾನಿ ತು ಭಕ್ತಿತಃ॥ ಇತಿ।

ea828ed132.d:
Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy or majjari Narasimha Reddy, son of a pALEyagAra, was executed in Koilkuntla in front of a crowd of over 2000 people.

He and his commander-in-chief Vadde Obanna were at the heart of the rebellion against British in 1847, where 5,000 peasants rose up against the British East India Company in Kurnool district, Rayalaseema Region of Andhra Pradesh. They were protesting against the changes introduced by the British to the traditional agrarian system in the first half of the nineteenth century. British kept his head on the fort wall in public view until 1877.

ಶರತ್ಕಾಲೇ ಮಹಾಪೂಜಾ ಕ್ರಿಯತೇ ಯಾ ಚ ವಾರ್ಷಿಕೀ।

eb4a86381d.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between aṅgārakaḥ and śukraḥ in pūrvāṣāḍhā dhanuḥ, center-to-center separation 0°10′25.76″.
eb4a86381d.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°10′25.76″, 0°10′18.94″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°56′03.09″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.08, elongation 0°59′32.91″ E). śukraḥ at pūrvāṣāḍhā-4 dhanuḥ (latitude 0°45′37.33″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 0°49′52.42″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here aṅgārakaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
eb4a86381d.s:

eb8d7f9289.b: Observed on Śukla-Caturthī tithi of Bhādrapadaḥ (lunar) month (Madhyāhnaḥ/puurvaviddha).
eb8d7f9289.s:
ಸುಮನ್ತುರುವಾಚ---  
ಶಿವಾ ಶಾನ್ತಾ ಸುಖಾ ರಾಜಂಶ್ಚತುರ್ಥೀ ತ್ರಿವಿಧಾ ಸ್ಮೃತಾ।   
ಮಾಸಿ ಭಾದ್ರಪದೇ ಶುಕ್ಲಾ ಶಿವಾ ಲೋಕೇಷು ಪೂಜಿತಾ॥೧॥   
ತಸ್ಯಾಂ ಸ್ನಾನಂ ತಥಾ ದಾನಮುಪವಾಸೋ ಜಪಸ್ತಥಾ।   
ಕ್ರಿಯಮಾಣಂ ಶತಗುಣಂ ಪ್ರಸಾದಾದ್ದನ್ತಿನೋ ನೃಪ॥೨॥   
ಗುಡಲವಣಘೃತಾನಾಂ ತು ದಾನಂ ಶುಭಕರಂ ಸ್ಮೃತಮ್।   
ಗುಡಾಪೂಪೈಸ್ತಥಾ ವೀರ ಪುಣ್ಯಂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಭೋಜನಮ್॥೩॥   
ಯಾಸ್ತಸ್ಯಾಂ ನರಶಾರ್ದೂಲ ಪೂಜಯನ್ತಿ ಸದಾ ಸ್ತ್ರಿಯಃ।   
ಗುಡಲವಣಪೂಪೈಶ್ಚ ಶ್ವಶ್ರೂಂ ಶ್ವಶುರಮೇವ ಚ॥೪॥   
ತಾಃ ಸರ್ವಾಃ ಸುಭಗಾಃ ಸ್ಯುರ್ವೈ ವಿಘ್ನೇಶಸ್ಯಾನುಮೋದನಾತ್।   
ಕನ್ಯಕಾ ತು ವಿಶೇಷೇಣ ವಿಧಿನಾಽನೇನ ಪೂಜಯೇತ್॥೫॥   
---ಶ್ರೀಭವಿಷ್ಯೇ ಮಹಾಪುರಾಣೇ ಶತಾರ್ಧಸಾಹಸ್ರ್ಯಾಂ ಸಂಹಿತಾಯಾಂ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮೇ ಪರ್ವಣಿ ಚತುರ್ಥೀಕಲ್ಪೇ ಸುಖಾವಹಾಙ್ಗಾರಕಚತುರ್ಥೀವ್ರತನಿರೂಪಣಂ ನಾಮೈಕತ್ರಿಂಶೋಽಧ್ಯಾಯತಃ  
ಅಸ್ಯಾಮೇವ ಚನ್ದ್ರದರ್ಶನೇ ದೋಷಮಾಹ ಪರಾಶರಃ---   
ಕನ್ಯಾದಿತ್ಯೇ ಚತುರ್ಥ್ಯಾಂ ಚ ಶುಕ್ಲೇ ಚನ್ದ್ರಸ್ಯ ದರ್ಶನಮ್।   
ಮಿಥ್ಯಾಭಿದೂಷಣಂ ಕುರ್ಯಾತ್ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಪಶ್ಯೇನ್ನ ತಂ ಸದಾ॥   
ತದ್ದೋಷಶಾನ್ತಯೇ ಮನ್ತ್ರೋ ವಿಷ್ಣುಪುರಾಣೇ---   
ಸಿಹಃ ಪ್ರಸೇನಮವಧೀತ್ ಸಿಂಹೋ ಜಾಮ್ಬವತಾ ಹತಃ।   
ಸುಕುಮಾರಕ ಮಾ ರೋದೀಸ್ತವ ಹ್ಯೇಷಃ ಸ್ಯಮನ್ತಕಃ॥

Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

ec05155e57.d: The boy Īśvara, son of Ujjvala bhaṭṭa of Karnataka, known as Cidghana, who approached Sureśvara and acquired the knowledge of bhāṣyas etc., having got his (Sureśvara’s) responsibility and remaining in the Pīṭha there, this Cidghana spent forty-five years as if Śiva Himself had come there to grant liberation to those who seek liberation. Revered by the wise, Cidghana having placed Vātsyāyāna, the initiated who was hailed as Hari arrived from Milky Ocean, and imparting the precepts He had attained his form, the pure consciousness on the tenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Māgha in the year Virodhikṛt of the Kali era.
ec05155e57.s:

ಶ್ರೀಭಾಷ್ಯಾದ್ಯುಪಲಭ್ಯ ತಸ್ಯ ಚ ಧುರಾಮಾಸಾದ್ಯ ಪೀಠೇ ವಸನ್।  
ನಿನ್ಯೇ ತತ್ರ ಶಿವಾಃ (೪೫) ಸಮಾಃ ಶಿವ ಇವ ಶ್ರೇಯೋಽರ್ಥಿನಾಂ ದೇಹಿನಾಂ  
ದಾತುಂ ಶ್ರೇಯ ಉಪಾಗತೋಽಯಮಿವ ಯಃ ಶ್ರೀಚಿದ್ಘನಾಖ್ಯೋ ಬಭೌ॥೨೧॥  
ಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಂ ಕ್ಷೀರಸರಿತ್ತಟಾದ್ಧರಿರಿತಿ ಖ್ಯಾತಂ ಚ ವಾತ್ಸ್ಯಾಯನಂ  
ಪೀಠೇ ಸ್ವೇ ವಿನಿವೇಶ್ಯ ದತ್ತನಿಯಮಂ ಸಞ್ಚಾರ್ಯ ಚ ಪ್ರಕ್ರಿಯಾಮ್।  
ಕಲ್ಯಬ್ದೇ ಚ ವಿರೋಧಿಕೃತ್ಯನುತಪಃ ಶುದ್ಧೇ ದಶಮ್ಯಾಮಗಾತ್  
ಸ್ವಂ ರೂಪಂ ಪರಮಂ ಸುಧೀಶತನುತಃ ಶ್ರೀಚಿದ್ಘನಶ್ಚಿದ್ಘನಮ್॥೨೨॥  
—ಪುಣ್ಯಶ್ಲೋಕಮಞ್ಜರೀ

ec6d35ac64.d: Magnitude: 56% of the solar diameter is covered (parimāṇa ≈6.7 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 03:13►17:49 (from 4 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra punarvasuḥ/puṣyaḥ/āśrēṣā (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or anūrādhā (anujanma) or uttaraprōṣṭhapadā (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: karkaṭaḥ, siṁhaḥ, dhanuḥ, mēṣaḥ get more ashubha phala, vr̥śchikaḥ, makaraḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam somewhat ashubha, kanyā, tulā, kumbhaḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

ec70bd8cca.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Kungiliya Kalaya Nayanmar, a Brahmana from Tirukadavur in the Chola kingdom, was renowned for his devotion to Bhagavan Shiva, symbolised by his constant burning of incense before the deity. The temple in Tirukadavur housed the Amrita Lingam, which originated from a pot of nectar transformed into a Lingam. The temple's deity, Amrita Ghateshwarar, was worshipped by Markandeya, leading to his immortality. The Devi of the temple, Abhirami Amman, was venerated by Abhirami Bhattar, whose devotion led to a miraculous transformation of the moon's phase.

Despite experiencing sudden poverty, Nayanmar continued his devotion, even selling his property to maintain his ritual of burning incense. One day, his wife, willing to support his devotion, offered her sacred Mangalyam to sell for food. However, when Nayanmar went to sell it, he was so captivated by the offer of high-quality incense from a hawker (Bhagavan Shiva in disguise) that he exchanged the Mangalyam for it, forgetting his family's hunger.

Bhagavan Shiva, impressed with the couple's devotion, blessed them with wealth. Nayanmar's wife prepared a meal and awaited his return. When Nayanmar went to the temple with the incense, Bhagavan Shiva appeared to him, acknowledging his devotion and instructing him to return home. Astonished, Nayanmar found his house transformed into a place of prosperity and shared his newfound wealth with other Shiva Bhaktas.

Nayanmar's devotion was further exemplified in Tiruppanandal (https://maps.app.goo.gl/Du84NWnVhaTQWMYE8), where he straightened the leaning Lingam of Arunasatesar, which had tilted to accept a garland from a devotee. Using a rope of divine love, Nayanmar miraculously righted the Lingam, a feat that astonished and earned him further reverence.

After spending more time serving Bhagavan Shiva and His devotees, Nayanmar eventually attained the divine abode, leaving a legacy of unwavering devotion and service to Bhagavan.
ec70bd8cca.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society

ecb57c7a24.d:
On this day, in the first battle on the neDuMkoTa coast-to-mountain fortification, Tipu Sultan and troops were routed. Tipu was wounded (physically and mentally), and lost 1k troops. padmanAbhapura lost 300. Several of Tipu's officers (including Europeans) were captured.

Two horses were shot from under Tipu, and he even got an arrow in the back. During the hasty retreat, Tipu fell back into the ditch twice before being helped out and the occasional lameness which he suffered until his death was reputedly the consequence. Tipu's sword, the palanquin, the dagger, the ring and many other personal effects fell into the ditch, and then into the hands of the minister keshava-dAsa.


Aftermath
Humiliated Tipu vowed to take down "the contemptible wall". The fine wall held up till 15th April. Then he managed a 1km wide breach after 1 month of sustained artillery fire and poured in - only to be foiled again at Alwaye river bank. He retreated by 24 May 1790 to defend his kingdom from British threat.

Context
The Dutch captive-turned general of padmanAbhapura's mArtANDa varma, De Lannoy, had built an excellent fortification from coast to mountain - neDuMkoTa. It had a 16 feet wide and 20 deep ditch. dharmarAja rAma varma had tried to get British help when Tipu's attack was imminent, but only got words. The Dutch, who'd sold forts to rAma varma helped a bit - by sending an engineer von Krause, who was dispatched to the wall. He wrote an account of the battle.

When Tipu attacked, he tried filling a small portion of the ditch with cotton sacks and moving in a small column via a narrow passage. At first the Mysoreans overpowered three batteries of the Lines but subsequently their flanks were subjected to fire from the woods. They were so surprised by the first round of fire that they fell into disorder. Then the well drilled nair army advanced and the confusion increased. Those Mysoreans who had not yet been trampled down by their horses while retreating found that the sacks with cotton, used for filling up the ditch when they set out, as well as some powder-barrels, had caught fire. This forced them to jump from the ramparts.

ecfe187da6.d:
On this day, vAnchinathan Iyer, inspired by  Subramaniam Aiyar and armed by Va Ve Su Iyer accomplice of nIlakaNTha brahmachAri of bhAratamAta-sangha with a gun sent by sAvarkar's accompalice Madam Cama of Paris Indian Society, shot dead a mlecCha collector Robert Ashe (who had successfully harrassed VO Chidambaram Pillai's Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company) before killing himself (after pushing away his peon Khadar bAdshAh). His letter:

- I dedicate my life as a small contribution to my motherland. I am alone responsible for this.
- The mlechas of England having captured our country, tread over the sanathana dharma of the Hindus and destroy them. Every Indian is trying to drive out the English and get swarajyam and restore sanathana dharma. Our Raman, Sivaji, Krishnan, Guru Govindan, Arjuna ruled our land protecting all dharmas, but in this land, they are making arrangements to crown George V, a mlecha, and one who eats the flesh of cows.
- Three thousand Madrasees have taken a vow to kill George V as soon as he lands in our country. In order to make others know our intention, I who am the least in the company, have done this deed this day. This is what everyone in Hindustan should consider it as his duty.
- I will kill Ashe, whose arrival here is to celebrate the crowning of cow-eater King George V in this glorious land which was once ruled by great samrats. This I do to make them understand the fate of those who cherish the thought of enslaving this sacred land.
- I, as the least of them, wish to warn George by killing Ashe. 
- Vande Mataram. Vande Mataram. Vande Mataram
- sd/-, R. Vanchi Aiyar, Shencottah

edbb08f944.s:
ಸ್ವಾತ್ಯಾಮಥ ಧನಂ ದತ್ತ್ವಾ ಯದಿಷ್ಟತಮಮಾತ್ಮನಃ ।  
ಪ್ರಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ಲೋಕಾನ್ಸ ಶುಭಾನಿಹ ಚೈವ ಮಹದ್ಯಶಃ॥೧೩-೯೯-೧೮॥  
ಭೀಷ್ಮ ಉವಾಚ  
ಯಮಸ್ತು ಯಾನಿ ಶ್ರಾದ್ಧಾನಿ ಪ್ರೋವಾಚ ಶಶಬಿನ್ದವೇ ।  
ತಾನಿ ಮೇ ಶೃಣು ಕಾಮ್ಯಾನಿ ನಕ್ಷತ್ರೇಷು ಪೃಥಕ್ಪೃಥಕ್॥೧೩-೧೩೬-೧॥  
ಚಿತ್ರಾಯಾಂ ತು ದದಚ್ಛ್ರಾದ್ಧಂ ಲಭೇದ್ರೂಪವತಃ ಸುತಾನ್ ।  
ಸ್ವಾತಿಯೋಗೇ ಪಿತೄನರ್ಚ್ಯ ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯಮುಪಜೀವತಿ॥೧೩-೧೩೬-೭॥  
---ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇ (ಕುಮ್ಭಘೋಣ-ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣಮ್)

edfcca4e60.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′14.97″.
edfcca4e60.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′14.97″, 0°59′05.31″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′49.80″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.60″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′34.83″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.82″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

ee8a20b416.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.52″.
ee8a20b416.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.52″, 0°41′02.15″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′24.21″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.65″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′14.69″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.52″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

eeae687033.b: Observed on Aśvinī nakshatra of Tulā (sidereal solar) month (Prātaḥ/paraviddha).
eeae687033.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

Tirumula Nayanmar, a revered Shaiva Siddha and one of the eight disciples of Tirunandi Devar, embarked on a journey to meet Agastya Rishi in the Pothia hills. Departing from Kailasa, he visited numerous Shaivite shrines and, upon reaching Tiruvavaduthurai, witnessed a herd of mourning cows beside their deceased herder, Mulan. To comfort the cows, Tirumula Nayanmar transferred his consciousness into Mulan's body, leaving his own physical form in a tree trunk.

Assuming Mulan's role, he herded the cows back to the village, where Mulan's wife, expecting her husband, was surprised by his changed demeanor. Declaring himself a changed person and advising her to seek spiritual liberation, Tirumula Nayanmar distanced himself from her, arousing the village's curiosity. Upon investigation, the villagers acknowledged his spiritual transformation and advised the wife to respect his new path.

Unable to retrieve his original body owing to Bhagavan Shiva's Lila, Tirumula Nayanmar, still in Mulan's form, dedicated himself to composing a seminal work on Shaiva Philosophy at Tiruvavaduthurai. He devoted himself to worshiping Bhagavan and settled beneath a nearby peepal tree, entering a state of deep meditation. He remained in this state of Samadhi for three millennia. However, each year, he momentarily emerged from this deep meditative state to compose a single verse. Over the span of three thousand years, this process led to the creation of three thousand verses, collectively forming the sacred text known as the Tirumandiram. Having accomplished his divine mission, Tirumula Nayanmar returned to Kailasa.

eedf5cbec5.s:
ಆಶ್ವಿನಸ್ಯ ಸಿತೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ದಶಮ್ಯಾಂ ತಾರಕೋದಯೇ।  
ಸ ಕಾಲೋ ವಿಜಯೋ ಜ್ಞೇಯಃ ಸರ್ವಕಾರ್ಯಾರ್ಥಸಿದ್ಧಯೇ॥ (ಜ್ಯೋತಿರ್ನಿಬನ್ಧಃ)  
ಸ್ಮೃತಿ-ಕೌಸ್ತುಭೇ---  
ಅಸ್ಯಾಮೇವ ದಶಮ್ಯಾಂ ವಿಜಯಮುಹೂರ್ತವ್ಯಾಪಿನ್ಯಾಂ ದೇಶಾನ್ತರಯಾತ್ರಾರ್ಥಿಭಿರ್ಯಾತ್ರಾ ವಿಧೇಯಾ---  
ಆಶ್ವಿನಸ್ಯ ಸಿತೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ದಶಮ್ಯಾಂ ಸರ್ವರಾತ್ರಿಷು।  
ಸಾಯಙ್ಕಾಲೇ ಶುಭಾ ಯಾತ್ರಾ ದಿವಾ ವಾ ವಿಜಯಕ್ಷಣೇ॥  
ಇತಿ ಭೃಗುವಚನಾತ್।  
ಸರ್ವೇತಿ ಚನ್ದ್ರಾನುಕೂಲ್ಯಂ ನಾಪೇಕ್ಷ್ಯಮಿತ್ಯಾಶಯಃ।  
ಈಷತ್ ಸನ್ಧ್ಯಾಮತಿಕ್ರಾನ್ತಃ ಕಿಞ್ಚಿದುದ್ಭಿನ್ನತಾರಕಃ।  
ವಿಜಯೋ ನಾಮ ಕಾಲೋಽಯಂ ಸರ್ವಕಾರ್ಯಾರ್ಥಸಾಧಕಃ॥  
ಇತಿ ಜ್ಯೋತಿ ಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೋಕ್ತವಿಜಯಮುಹೂರ್ತಾಭಿಪ್ರಾಯಂ ಸಾಯಮಿತಿ।  
ಏಕಾದಶೋ ಮುಹೂರ್ತೋಽಪಿ ವಿಜಯಃ ಪರಿಕೀರ್ತಿತಃ।  
ತಸ್ಮಿನ್ಸರ್ವೈರ್ವಿಧಾತವ್ಯಾ ಯಾತ್ರಾ ವಿಜಯಕಾಙ್ಕ್ಷಿಭಿಃ॥  
ಇತಿ ಭೃಗೂಕ್ತವಿಜಯಮುಹೂರ್ತಸ್ಯಾನುಕೂಲ್ಯತ್ವಾಶಯಂ ದಿವಾ ವೇತಿ।  
ಏಕಾದಶೀಯುಕ್ತೇ ಉಕ್ತಮುಹೂರ್ತೇಽಪಿ ಪ್ರಸ್ಥಾನಂ ನ ವಿಧೇಯಮ್।  
ದಶಮೀ ಯಃ ಸಮುಲ್ಲಙ್ಘ್ಯ ಪ್ರಸ್ಥಾನಂ ಕುರುತೇ ನರಃ।  
ತಸ್ಯ ಸಂವತ್ಸರಂ ರಾಜ್ಯೇ ನ ಕೋಽಪಿ ವಿಜಯೋ ಭವೇತ್॥  
ಇತಿ ಸ್ಕಾನ್ದನಿಷೇಧಾತ್।

ef33d7b448.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in śravaṇaḥ makaraḥ, center-to-center separation 0°41′09.62″.
ef33d7b448.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°41′09.62″, 0°41′02.25″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 2°00′24.64″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.28, elongation 5°47′39.39″ E). śukraḥ at śravaṇaḥ-4 makaraḥ (latitude 1°19′15.02″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.91, elongation 5°35′40.25″ E). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.

ef37457887.s:
ಸ್ಮೃತ್ಯನ್ತರೇ—  
ಕೃಷ್ಣಪಕ್ಷೇ ತೃತೀಯಾಯಾಂ ಫಾಲ್ಗುನಾಷಾಢಕಾರ್ತಿಕೇ।  
ಶುಕ್ಲಾಶ್ವಯುಗ್ದ್ವಿತೀಯಾಯಾಂ ನೈವಾಧ್ಯಾಯಂ ಸಮಾಚರೇತ್॥  
ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯುಕ್ತೋಽಪ್ಯನಧ್ಯಾಯೇ ನಾಧೀಯೀತ ಕದಾಚನ।

ef4d78fc26.s:
ಪುಷ್ಪಮಣ್ಡಪಿಕಾ ಕಾರ್ಯಾ ರಮ್ಭಾಸ್ತಮ್ಭೋಪಶೋಭಿತಾ।  
ತತ್ರ ಸಮ್ಪೂಜಯೇದ್ದೇವೀಂ ಶಕ್ತ್ಯಾ ಸ್ವರ್ಣಾದಿನಿರ್ಮಿತಾಮ್॥  
ವೇದೇಷು ಸರ್ವಶಾಸ್ತ್ರೇಷು ದಿವಿ ಭೂಮೌ ರಸಾತಲೇ।  
ಶ್ರುತೋ ದೃಷ್ಟಶ್ಚ ಬಹುಶೋ ನ ಶಕ್ತ್ಯಾ ರಹಿತಃ ಶಿವಃ।  
ತ್ವಂ ಶಕ್ಸ್ತಿಸ್ತ್ವಂ ಸ್ವಧಾ ಸ್ವಾಹಾ ತ್ವಂ ಸಾವಿತ್ರೀ ಸರಸ್ವತೀ।  
ಪತಿಂ ದೇಹಿ ಸುತಾನ್ದೇಹಿ ಗೃಹಂ ದೇವಿ ನಮೋಽಸ್ತು ತೇ॥  
ಯೋಷಿತಃ ಪುರುಷೋ ವಾಽಪಿ ಖ್ಯಾತಂ ರಮ್ಭಾವ್ರತಂ ಭುವಿ।  
ಭಾರ್ಯಾಂ ಪುತ್ರಂ ಗೃಹಂ ಭೋಗಾನ್ ಕುಲವೃದ್ಧಿಮವಾಪ್ನುಯುಃ॥  
-ಸ್ಮೃತಿ-ಕೌಸ್ತುಭಃ  
ಸಾ ಪೂರ್ವವಿದ್ಧಾ ಗ್ರಾಹ್ಯಾ।

ef5a78b4ef.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈4.1 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
ef5a78b4ef.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.34 (parimāṇa ≈4.1 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:32►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
ef5a78b4ef.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

efc59ef534.d:
As stated in the Mahābhārata:
- Observance: Pitṛ-gāthā: pāyasa with ghee on trayodaśī in Maghā in dakṣiṇāyana (MBh 13.135.11, 13.135.12, 13.135.13)
efc59ef534.s:
ಗಾಥಾಶ್ಚಾಪ್ಯತ್ರ ಗಾಯನ್ತಿ ಪಿತೃಗೀತಾ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರ ।  
ಸನತ್ಕುಮಾರೋ ಭಗವಾನ್ಪುರಾ ಮಯ್ಯಭ್ಯಭಾಷತ॥೧೩-೧೩೫-೧೧॥  
ಅಪಿ ನಃ ಸ್ವಕುಲೇ ಜಾಯಾದ್ಯೋ ನೋ ದದ್ಯಾತ್ತ್ರಯೋದಶೀಮ್ ।  
ಮಘಾಸು ಸರ್ಪಿಃಸಂಯುಕ್ತಂ ಪಾಯಸಂ ದಕ್ಷಿಣಾಯನೇ॥೧೩-೧೩೫-೧೨॥  
ಆಜೇನ ವಾಽಪಿ ಲೌಹೇನ ಮಘಾಸ್ವೇವ ಯತವ್ರತಃ ।  
ಹಸ್ತಿಚ್ಛಾಯಾಸು ವಿಧಿವತ್ಕರ್ಣವ್ಯಜನವೀಜಿತಮ್॥೧೩-೧೩೫-೧೩॥  
---ಮಹಾಭಾರತೇ (ಕುಮ್ಭಘೋಣ-ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣಮ್)

efcbfa9a21.s:

ಯದಾ ಸಙ್ಕ್ಲೇಶಿತೋ ಮರ್ತ್ಯೋ ನಾನಾದುಃಖೈಶ್ಚ ದಾರುಣೈಃ।

ವನ್ದೇ ವಾರಾಹವಕ್ತ್ರಾಂ ವರಮಣಿಮಕುಟಾಂ ವಿದ್ರುಮಶ್ರೋತ್ರಭೂಷಾಮ್  
ಹಾರಾಗ್ರೈವೇಯತುಙ್ಗಸ್ತನಭರನಮಿತಾಂ ಪೀತಕೌಶೇಯವಸ್ತ್ರಾಮ್।  
ದೇವೀಂ ದಕ್ಷೋಧ್ವಹಸ್ತೇ ಮುಸಲಮಥಪರಂ ಲಾಙ್ಗಲಂ ವಾ ಕಪಾಲಮ್  
ವಾಮಾಭ್ಯಾಂ ಧಾರಯನ್ತೀಂ ಕುವಲಯಕಲಿತಾಂ ಶ್ಯಾಮಲಾಂ ಸುಪ್ರಸನ್ನಾಮ್॥

efe43b825e.b: Graha-yuddha (amshu-vimarda) between budhaḥ and śukraḥ in viśākhā tulā, center-to-center separation 0°59′14.95″.
efe43b825e.d:
This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°59′14.95″, 0°59′05.29″ apart, disc-to-disc. budhaḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 1°53′49.76″ N, vakra (retrograde), magnitude +2.08, elongation 10°27′48.60″ W). śukraḥ at viśākhā-3 tulā (latitude 0°54′34.82″ N, Rju (direct), magnitude -3.92, elongation 10°19′53.83″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) śukraḥ is taken as jayI over budhaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
efe43b825e.s:
ಭಾವಾಭಾವಾಯ ಲೋಕಾನಾಂ ಕಲ್ಪನೇಯಂ ಪ್ರದರ್ಶಿತಾ।  
ಸ್ವಮಾರ್ಗಗಾಃ ಪ್ರಯಾನ್ತ್ಯೇತೇ ದೂರಮನ್ಯೋನ್ಯಮಾಶ್ರಿತಾಃ॥  
--ಸೂರ್ಯಸಿದ್ಧಾನ್ತೇ  
  
ಷಣ್ಮಾಸಂ ಗ್ರಹಭಿನ್ನಭಂ ತ್ಯಜ ಶುಭೇ ಯೌದ್ಧಂ ತಥೋತ್ಪಾತಭಮ್।  
--ಮುಹೂರ್ತಚಿನ್ತಾಮಣೌ (ನಾರದಸಂಹಿತಾನುಸಾರೇಣ)

efebe6a374.b: Observed on Amāvāsyā tithi of Dhanuḥ (sidereal solar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
efebe6a374.s:
ಆಶ್ವಿನಸ್ಯಾಸಿತೇ ಪಕ್ಷೇ ಭೂತಾಯಾಂ ಚ ಮಹಾನಿಶಿ।  
ಭೌಮವಾರೇಽಞ್ಜನಾದೇವೀ ಹನೂಮನ್ತಮಜೀಜನತ್॥ (ವ್ರತರತ್ನಾಕರಮ್)

efec373932.d: Guruḥ emerges from combustion into bAlya (infancy) on 2025-Jul-08 10:35. At this moment guruḥ is at ārdrā-2 mithunam (latitude 0°07′05.08″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.89, elongation 9°51′31.20″ W of the Sun. A graha in bAlya is likewise considered to give reduced results, for 15 days, before regaining its full strength.

eff1e1faeb.d: Śukraḥ emerges from combustion into bAlya (infancy) on 2027-Sep-10 19:37. At this moment śukraḥ is at uttaraphalgunī-2 kanyā (latitude 1°20′30.22″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -3.91, elongation 8°18′13.89″ E of the Sun. A graha in bAlya is likewise considered to give reduced results, for 5 days, before regaining its full strength.

eff4e0fa65.d: Budhaḥ sets into combustion (astamayaH), heading prāk (east), on 2027-Mar-22 09:29. At this moment budhaḥ is at śatabhiṣak-2 kumbhaḥ (latitude 1°37′53.42″ S, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude +0.15, elongation 27°03′44.00″ W of the Sun. Combustion (mAudhyam) is generally considered to weaken a graha's ability to give full results in its significations; undertakings connected with budhaḥ are traditionally best avoided until it re-emerges.

effed99ff4.b: Observed on Śukla-Aṣṭamī tithi of Caitraḥ (lunar) month (Sūryōdayaḥ/puurvaviddha).
effed99ff4.s:
ಸ್ಕಾನ್ದೇ---  
ಚೈತ್ರೇ ಮಾಸಿ ಸಿತಾಷ್ಟಮ್ಯಾಂ ಯೋ ನರೋ ನಿಯತೇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಃ।  
ಸ್ನಾಯಾಲ್ಲೌಹಿತ್ಯತೋಯೇಷು ಸ ಯಾತಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಣಃ ಪದಮ್॥  
ಲೌಹಿತ್ಯೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪುತ್ರಃ। ತತ್ರ ಸಙ್ಕಲ್ಪಃ---  
ಓಮದ್ಯೇತ್ಯಾದಿ ಸರ್ವಪಾಪಕ್ಷಯಪೂರ್ವಕಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪದಗಮನಕಾಮೋ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪುತ್ರಸ್ನಾನಮಹಂ ಕರಿಷ್ಯೇ ಇತಿ।  
ಓಂ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮಪುತ್ರ ಮಹಾಭಾಗ ಶನ್ತನೋಃ ಕುಲಸಮ್ಭವ।  
ಅಮೋಘಾಗರ್ಭಸಮ್ಭತ ಪಾಪಂ ಲೌಹಿತ್ಯ ಮೇ ಹರ॥  
ಇತಿ ಪಠಿತ್ವಾ ಸ್ನಾಯಾತ್।

efff57b234.d: Guruḥ enters vArdhakya (old age) on 2026-Jul-01 00:02, 15 days before it sets into combustion (mAudhyam). At this moment guruḥ is at puṣyaḥ-1 karkaṭaḥ (latitude 0°26′18.68″ N, moving r̥ju (direct)), magnitude -1.81, elongation 21°07′52.21″ E of the Sun. A graha in vArdhakya is considered weakened, giving reduced results, though less so than in outright mAudhya.
